A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEPS and support comparison of their text, equations, tables and figures. All v1 appendices A–C were inspected; v2 ends with references and contains no appendix. Renamed modules and relocated experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original SEPS retrieval results, component ablations, hyperparameter experiments and qualitative analyses, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original retrieval experiments and reports additional transfer, visual-grounding, computational-cost and ablation results.

M1.justification: Equation 3 changes from one combined significance score to separate sparse- and dense-guided scores, with different predictor and attention weights. This is a local procedural revision beyond renaming SDTPS to DGSC and HRPA to SGMA; aggregation, alignment scoring and losses largely remain unchanged. Table 4 also introduces a Grad-CAM proposal-selection adaptation for grounding.

E1.justification: V2 adds Flickr30K-to-MS-COCO zero-shot retrieval and referring-expression grounding on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg. These introduce distribution-shift and localization scenarios beyond v1's retrieval evaluation. Table 7 additionally tests mismatched dense descriptions from other images and datasets.

E2.justification: The VLP comparison loses the entire UNITER, ViLT, SOHO, ALBEF and BLIP group from v1 Appendix A, Table 3. V2 Table 2 retains only the CLIP-backbone comparisons with CLIP, VSE++, SCAN, LAPS and SEPS. The main Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include transferring Flickr30K-trained CLIP ViT-B/16 models without target fine-tuning, selecting grounding proposals through Grad-CAM, and measuring per-pair inference latency on one NVIDIA A100. Dense-source and MLLM-configuration controls are also added. Existing retrieval splits, recall metrics and five-fold MS-COCO averaging remain unchanged; omitted training settings do not establish changed training.

E4.justification: V2 adds concatenation and score-sum fusion ablations, matched versus mismatched dense-text controls, comparisons across six MLLMs, transfer tests and computational-cost analysis. V1's three incremental-component ablations and Appendix C qualitative patch-selection/alignment cases disappear. The existing hyperparameter plots remain, despite removal of their detailed appendix tables.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging MS-COCO 1K results over five folds. Neither reports training-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 and the retained CLIP comparison scores are identical. However, matching ablation rows change: complete-SEPS image-to-text R@5 changes from 96.7 in v1 Table 2 to 93.7 in v2 Table 5, and without-aggregation text-to-image R@1 changes from 84.7 to 83.7. V2 adds substantial transfer, grounding, cost and control results, while removing VLP comparison rows and detailed sensitivity recall entries.

T1.justification: Equation 3 substantively revises the mathematical definition of patch significance through separate branch scores and changed weighting. The newly written Gumbel-Softmax equation explains an existing technique. No new theorem or proof accompanies the semantic-consensus terminology.

C1.justification: The central claims about combining dense/sparse guidance and relevance-aware alignment for improved retrieval remain. V2 removes the first-systematic-framework claim and the explicit 23%–86% rSum improvement claims, reframes the contribution around Semantic Sparsity Bias, and adds robust zero-shot generalization to the conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations linking transfer to intrinsic semantic correspondences, weak naive fusion to semantic drift, and saturation near LLaVA-13B to architectural benefits. It also argues that measured overhead permits practical deployment. The Impact Statement expands v1's demographic-bias limitation to hallucinated attributes, privacy-sensitive inferences and surveillance/profiling risks, while detailed appendix interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's implementation section specifying the generation prompt, decoding settings, 30 epochs, AdamW, batch size, learning rate, loss margin and default selection coefficients. It adds beta=0.6, min-max normalization and A100 timing information, but these only partly replace the lost detail. The GitHub link remains; the separate disclosure of access to training/evaluation logs and checkpoints is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning around Semantic Sparsity Bias and a structure-centric alternative to representation enhancement. It adds hallucination, transfer and grounding literature, including HalluLens, HALoGEN, ReCLIP and Grad-CAM, while removing PCME and the standalone VLP references. Attribution of the aggregation network to Zong et al. also disappears, although the aggregation formula remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and much of the methodology are extensively rewritten around new terminology, including DGSC, SGMA and Holistic Visual-Linguistic Anchor. Experimental discussion is reorganized, selected appendix results move into the main text, and the implementation, reproducibility and appendix sections disappear. Conference-header and author-format presentation also change.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a two-column layout, substantially redraws the architecture diagram, revises Figure 1 and restructures the ablation table. The reduced CLIP table moves into the main text, four new experimental tables and an MLLM radar plot appear, and the detailed sensitivity tables and qualitative figures are removed. Figure 3 largely preserves the existing plots.

improvement.justification: The added transfer, grounding and diagnostic experiments provide useful evidence, and removing v1's misleading rSum percentage-gain wording improves claim precision. However, v2 loses substantial reproducibility detail, five VLP comparators and qualitative evidence. Its new claim of consistent grounding superiority also conflicts with Table 4: SCAN scores 44.4 versus SEPS's 43.4 on RefCOCO TestB. These material gains and losses leave the net direction of overall quality unclear.
